article.Citation/Title: Smart, R. G., & Storm, T. (1964). The efficacy of LSD in the treatment of alcoholism. Quarterly Journal of Studies on Alcohol, 25, 333-338.
article.SourcePDF: alcohol/Smart, R. G., & Storm, T. (1964). The efficacy of LSD in the treatment of alcoholism.pdf
article.EligibilityNote: Smart & Storm conducted no trial of their own; this is a narrative methodological critique, published under 'NOTES and COMMENT,' of five prior LSD-alcoholism studies (Smith 1958; Chwelos et al. 1959; MacLean et al. 1961; Chandler & Hartman 1960; Eisner & Cohen 1958). No participants enrolled, no intervention administered. Fails criterion (a).

article.Outcome: No primary outcome belongs to this article. Smart & Storm ran no trial; the numeric findings in the text (e.g., 12/24, 15/16, 46/61 alcoholics 'improved'/'much improved') are the reviewed studies' own reported outcomes (refs 5-7), not this article's. Coded '.'.
article.SD: No dispersion/test statistic of the authors' own exists to pair with an Outcome; none was computed for a study that does not exist. Coded '.'.
article.PVal: No p-value is reported for an analysis conducted by these authors; none was run. Coded '.'.
article.SampleSize_NFinal: No analytic sample belongs to this article. The article discusses other studies' samples (e.g., 24, 16, 61, 17, 3 patients) but has no N of its own. Coded '.'.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: This is a narrative commentary, not an empirical study. 'objective' is met (stated aim: 'to examine closely the studies purporting to show that LSD is a useful adjunct to therapy'). 'design' is met because the review's own evaluative framework is described — three requirements: control groups, blind administration/scoring, and pre/post measures — applied to the five reviewed studies. 'results' is met via the SUMMARY section stating the review's findings (none of the five studies used control groups or blinding; only one reported comparable pre/post measures, and even that one used different pre- and post-treatment instruments). Setting, eligibility, intervention, comparator, outcomes, sample-size/power, randomization, blinding, statistical methods, harms and funding/COI are all N because no trial of the authors' own exists for any of these elements to describe.

article.Pos Result Y/N: Coded 3 (cannot be determined) — there is no intervention or trial conducted by these authors whose direction of effect could be judged; the article's own conclusion is a critique of methodology, not a treatment-effect finding.
article.RandomizationYN: Coded 3 — the concept is genuinely inapplicable: no trial or participants belong to this article. The text discusses the absence of randomization in the five reviewed (other) studies, not in a design of its own.
article.BlindingYN: Coded 3 for the same reason as RandomizationYN — no trial of the authors' own exists in which blinding could have been implemented.
article.Double+Blind: Coded 3, consistent with BlindingYN=3 (not 1, per the 'must not be 1 when BlindingYN=0' rule and the broader inapplicability of the concept here).
article.Comparator: Coded 3 — no comparator or control group exists because no trial was conducted by these authors.
article.PrimaryCare: Coded 3 — the article is a methodological commentary, not a clinical-care or intervention study that could interface with primary-care settings.
article.Power: Coded 3 — no statistical power analysis, a priori or post hoc, exists for a study the authors did not conduct. (The article does discuss general research standards but performs no power analysis of its own.)
article.Retention (%): Coded '.' — not calculable; there is no completer/denominator pair belonging to this article's own sample, because there is no sample.

article.HarmsAssessed: Coded 3, consistent with SafetyReported='N' (permitted values 0/3/'.' ). No trial exists in which harms could have been assessed; the article's discussion of 'placebo reactors' is a citation of others' literature, not an AE assessment of its own.
article.Followup in months: Coded '.' — no follow-up was conducted by these authors. The article critiques the wide, inconsistent follow-up intervals used across the five reviewed studies (ranging roughly 2 months to 3 years) but performed no follow-up of its own.
article.BehaviorChangeMeasured: Coded 0, not 1 — no measurement was performed by these authors; they synthesize behavior-change findings (drinking histories, 'improved'/'much improved' ratings) reported in five OTHER trials. The same reasoning (no measurement performed by these authors) applies to PhysicalChangeMeasured, MentalHealthChangeMeasured, QualityOfLifeMeasured, Implementation Outcome, ReductionMeasured, CessationMeasured, RelapseMeasured and MortalityMeasured, each coded 0.
article.LSD: Coded 0, not 1 — substance flags are intervention flags, not exposure/topic flags. Smart & Storm administered no LSD; they critique LSD's use in five OTHER trials (Smith 1958; Chwelos et al. 1959; MacLean et al. 1961; Chandler & Hartman 1960; Eisner & Cohen 1958). No substance flag is set on this record for the same reason.
article.SafetyReported: Coded 'N' — the article performs no AE/safety assessment of its own study (there is no study); its discussion of 'placebo reactors' and symptom overlap is drawn from the cited psychopharmacology literature (refs 11-14), not from an AE assessment conducted here.
article.AE_denominator: Coded '.' (per spec, never 'NA') — no safety-assessed population exists because no trial was conducted by these authors.
article.ArmScope: 'NA' — no arms exist; the article is not a trial and has no exposed population.
article.WorstSeverity: 'NA' because SafetyReported='N'; no severity scale applies.
article.EligibleYN: Coded 'N'. Under the eligibility screen's criterion (a), a clinical trial requires 'a prospectively planned intervention administered to participants for research purposes, with defined enrollment, an assigned regimen, and prospective outcome assessment.' This article is explicitly a critique/commentary (section header 'NOTES and COMMENT') that evaluates five OTHER published trials against methodological standards (control groups, blinding, pre/post measurement); the authors enrolled no participants and administered no intervention. Criterion (a) fails; EligibilityFailedCriterion='not_clinical_trial'.

config_proposal.note: Smart & Storm 1964 is a methodological critique of five prior LSD-alcoholism trials, not a clinical trial of its own; it reports no effect size, test statistic, or sample of its own to convert. No defensible Tier-1 conversion exists.
config_proposal.tier2_basis: No empirical data of the authors' own — the article is a narrative commentary evaluating other studies' methodology, not a study reporting a treatment effect.
